newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds surge across the broad.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds surge across the broad.

text.p: Israeli bonds surged broadly on Monday for the third consecutive session on hopes for declining inflation, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.15 pct to 105.01
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 to 103.91
Volume was a low 129 million shekels.
"The market was rising across the board today as investors believe that inflation will decline in 1997 as the economy is experiencing a slowdown," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.
"Bonds were showing strength today, rising sharply as investors put more money into saving plans which have to buy bonds," said Shahar Gazit at Batucha Securities and Investments.

Traders said that long CPI-linked bonds rose sharply. "Long bonds were leading today's rise as investors hope that lower inflation will lead the Bank of Israel to lower its key lending rate," the Discount trader said.
Traders noted that long inflation-linked bonds with terms of 10 to 15 years rocketed 0.73 percent. "This must be a mistake... someone simply gave a wrong limit," the Discount trader said.
"Unlinked bonds were also rising sharply with yields falling further towards four percent. If the inflation declines these bonds will become more attractive," he said.
Gazit added that yields on the Makam, which is also unlinked, fell to 13.5 percent which is relatively low.

Dollar-linked bonds were the main gainers following the sharp decline of the shekel against the dollar. In local trading the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3810 shekels against 3.3610 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
